Using REFERENCE_0 as the rough composition guide and REFERENCE_1 as the cleaned pose/layout guide, turn the sketch into a polished full-color anime manga panel. Keep the same 4-character arrangement and poses: 1 large muscular student centered in back flexing, 1 blond student on the right flexing, 1 small white-haired student on the left in a crouched power pose, and 1 red-haired character cropped large in the lower-left foreground reacting in shock. Replace the rough construction lines with clean inked line art, cel shading, and finished school-uniform colors. Create a realistic, front-facing waist-up portrait photo of a {argument name="profession" default="female nurse or clinician"} standing against a plain off-white textured wall. The subject wears {argument name="scrub color" default="burgundy"} V-neck medical scrubs with short sleeves, a small chest pocket on the viewer's right, and a metal snap detail near the collar. A detailed stethoscope hangs naturally around the neck, with black tubing, silver metal binaurals, gray eartips resting near the pocket, and the round chest piece visible on the viewer's left side. The person has medium brown hair tied back with a few loose strands near the ears, neutral upright posture, shoulders squared, centered composition, cropped from just above the head to mid-torso. The face is intentionally covered by a large square skin-tone privacy mosaic block, hiding all facial features while leaving the hair, ears, neck, clothing, and stethoscope visible. Use soft even indoor lighting, sharp photographic detail, natural colors, minimal background distractions, and a clean clinical profile-photo style.

Create a cinematic ultra-wide low-angle action photograph inside a dimly lit {argument name="room type" default="hotel bedroom"}, looking up from the surface of a messy white bed as {argument name="number of people" default="two"} energetic {argument name="subjects" default="young women"} jump high above the mattress. The larger subject on the right is frozen midair with knees bent, arms spread wide, bare feet visible, long dark hair flinging upward in wild strands, wearing a white sleeveless cropped top and pale yellow shorts. The smaller subject on the left is also jumping on the bed with arms raised, messy dark hair in motion, wearing a yellow camisole with white lace trim and blue denim shorts. Keep both faces indistinct or softly obscured by motion and shadow while emphasizing body movement, flying hair, and playful energy. Use dramatic warm hotel lighting: a bright backlight behind the jumpers creates glowing rim light, lens flare, dust particles in the air, and strong silhouettes; bedside lamps glow warmly on both sides, with curtains on the right, a framed picture on the left wall, dark headboard, rumpled white sheets, and large pillows in the foreground. Make the camera feel very close to the bed with a 24mm wide-angle perspective, dynamic diagonal composition, slight fisheye distortion, shallow depth of field, high ISO film grain, realistic skin tones, crisp fabric texture, motion blur on hair and limbs, and a spontaneous candid snapshot mood. Style: {argument name="visual style" default="photorealistic cinematic editorial photography"}, warm shadows, high contrast, chaotic joyful atmosphere, no text, no watermark.

Using REFERENCE_0 as the rough composition guide and REFERENCE_1 as the character/pose guide, turn the sketch into a polished, high-energy manga/anime illustration. Keep the same 4-character arrangement: 1 huge muscular student centered in back flexing one arm, 1 small white-haired student at lower left in a crouched/action pose, 1 slim standing student at right raising a fist, and 1 shocked pink-haired close-up face cropped at the bottom left. Preserve the school-uniform theme from REFERENCE_1 but render it as finished clothing: mint sweater and teal skirt styling for the center and left characters, a dark fitted uniform for the right character, and a close-up shocked face in the lower-left foreground. Use a dynamic shonen-comedy manga page style with thick outlines, dramatic motion lines, saturated colors, and layered comic effects.

Create a polished anime-style personification of {argument name="AI character name" default="ChatGPT"} as a gentle young female AI companion in a warm sunlit study. She has short silvery-white bobbed hair with soft waves, small braids, teal gradient tips, and teal OpenAI-knot hair ornaments with ribbons; her face is covered by a centered plain beige square censor block. She wears an elegant white academic robe with wide sleeves lined in teal, black inner dress or vest, teal tie, gold trim, small tech-like pins, and a teal ribbon emblem on one sleeve. She sits at a wooden desk, holding a dark book against her chest with the words “Knowledge Understanding Inspiration” and a small OpenAI-style knot symbol on the cover, while her other hand is raised as if presenting a hologram. To her left floats one translucent cyan chat bubble labeled “ChatGPT” with the text “Your AI companion. Here to help, inspire, and understand.” plus a small heart, and three smaller glowing square icons around it: one light bulb icon, one magnifying glass icon, and one chat message icon. On the desk include exactly eight visible study objects: a dark mug with an OpenAI-style knot logo and the word “ChatGPT,” a stack of four labeled books reading “Science,” “History,” “Art,” and “Philosophy,” one teal pen, one open notebook, one black book held by the character, and one small white robot mascot with teal glowing eyes and an OpenAI-style logo. The open notebook has two pages: the left page titled “Ideas” with notes “Conversations,” “Possibilities,” and “Infinite,” and the right page titled “Today’s Plan” with checklist items “Help someone,” “Spark ideas,” and “Make a difference,” with small doodles and hearts. In the background, show a cozy library with bookshelves, potted plants, sunlight streaming through a window, and a dark chalkboard. The chalkboard displays an OpenAI-style knot symbol and the phrase “Together, we can:” followed by exactly five bullet points: “Learn,” “Create,” “Solve,” “Explore,” and “and more!” plus little star doodles and a cat face doodle. Use a soft painterly anime illustration style, luminous rim lighting, teal and cream color palette, delicate highlights, high detail, shallow depth of field, cozy optimistic atmosphere, vertical composition.

01 Frontend (the part users see)

What it is: The interface that users can see, click, and interact with.
Where it is: Interfaces for websites, mini-programs, and apps.
Tools: HTML (structure), CSS (styling), JavaScript (interaction).

02 Backend (the processing part behind the scenes)

What it is: The brain behind the scenes, responsible for logic and calculation.
Where it is: On the server, invisible to users.
Function:
Handles login and registration
Calculates prices and recommends products
Receives frontend requests and returns data
Common languages: Java, Python, Go, JavaScript (Node.js)

03 Database (the memory part)

What it is: Used to store and manage data.
What it stores: Accounts, passwords, orders, inventory...
Common databases:
MySQL, PostgreSQL (relational, like tables)
MongoDB (document-based, like folders)

04 SaaS (Software as a Service)

What it is: SaaS = Software as a Service.
Core features:
Usable via web, mini-program, or app
Monthly or annual subscription
Common forms: Websites, mobile apps, and mini-programs can all be SaaS.

05 Summary

Frontend: User-visible interface
Backend: Logic and calculation behind the scenes
Database: Storage and management of data
SaaS: Delivering software as a service over the network
Frontend display → Backend processing → Database storage → SaaS delivery method

Someone who cannot draw, using a mouse in MS Paint, randomly doodling and writing text at the same time — messy, awkward, low-effort, but unexpectedly funny.

————————
Input Structure:

Image 1: Character reference (may include one or multiple subjects such as people, pets, or combinations)
Image 2: Layout reference (only for understanding the 4x4 grid structure, not style)

User Inputs:
- Text content (multiple lines, any language, may be fewer or more than 16)

————————
Character Usage Rules:

- Distribution should feel natural and context-driven

————————
Consistency Definition (Critical Redefinition):

This task prioritizes “consistent imperfection”, NOT realistic consistency.

The same character across stickers:
Does NOT need to look identical,
but must feel like it was drawn by the same unskilled person.

Must be consistent in:
- Drawing behavior (same clumsy hand)
- Simplification logic
- Error patterns (crooked proportions, shaky lines)
- Overall messiness level

Allowed:
- Facial distortion
- Proportion inconsistency
- Structural errors
- Missing details

Must retain:
- Minimal recognizable traits (e.g. silhouette, color, signature features)

Summary:
Consistency = “wrong in the same way”, not “accurate likeness”

————————
Layout & Structure:

- 16 stickers total, arranged in a 4x4 grid
- Each sticker is an independent frame
- Can feature single or multiple characters
- Individual frames can be messy
- Overall grid must remain clear and readable

————————
Text System (Core Expression Layer):

User provides multiple lines of text:

Quantity Handling:
- If fewer than 16 → automatically complete to 16
- If more than 16 → select the most expressive 16

Language Rule:
- Use the same language as the user input
- Do NOT enforce any specific language

Completion Rules:
- Maintain tone consistency (sarcastic, lazy, emotional, clingy, absurd, etc.)
- Prefer internet-style expressions
- Short phrases preferred, but longer lines allowed
- Avoid repetition

Expression Goals:
- Instantly understandable
- Emotionally strong
- Feels like real meme text

Tone Priority:
- Complaints
- Self-talk
- Emotional bursts
- Indifference / annoyance / absurd humor

Avoid:
- Polite responses
- Formal or structured phrasing

————————
Text-Image Integration (Critical):

Text must be DRAWN, not typeset.

Must:
- Look like mouse handwriting (crooked, shaky, uneven size)
- Be messy (tilted, overlapping, misaligned)
- Have inconsistent spacing
- Be placed freely (on face, beside, edges, etc.)

Allowed:
- Repeated letters (aaaaa)
- Stretched words (soooo tired)
- Random punctuation (????!!!)
- Messy or ugly writing

Must:
- Remain readable
- Not block understanding

————————
Expression Generation Mechanism (Most Important):

Simulate this process:

“A person who cannot draw, using a mouse, doodling randomly while writing text at the same time.”

Key Rules:
- Image and text must come from the SAME moment
- Not: draw first, then add text
- But: draw and write simultaneously

Each sticker should feel like:
- Random doodle
- Then spontaneous writing
- Or both happening together

Should feel:
- Unplanned
- Careless
- Immediate

————————
Text-Image Relationship:

Text and visuals should form:
- Commentary
- Emotional amplification
- Self-talk
- Or slightly mismatched humor

Allowed:
- Loose or imperfect alignment
- Absurd or off-topic humor

Goal:
Not accuracy, but humor

————————
Aesthetic DNA (Core Style Driver):

Style origin:
Terrible MS Paint doodles + failed imitation + extremely low drawing skill

Visual Traits:

Lines:
- Shaky, unstable, jagged
- Mouse-drawn look

Forms:
- Bad proportions
- Stick figures or crude shapes
- Distorted structures

Details:
- Minimal or none
- “Cannot draw” feeling

Texture:
- Pixelated
- Rough edges

Composition:
- Frames can be messy
- Grid must stay readable

Emotion:
- Awkward, direct, absurd, funny

Resemblance:
- Only vaguely resembles the original
- Like a failed copy

————————
Style Enforcement (Critical):

When conflict occurs:

Realism vs Style → ALWAYS choose Style

Allowed to break:
- Detail
- Proportion
- Accuracy
- Cleanliness

Strictly forbid:
- Clean lines
- Correct anatomy
- Polished visuals
- Designed aesthetics

Rule:
If it looks “good”, it is WRONG.

Force it back to messy, ugly, low-effort.

————————
Anti-Template & Randomization System (Critical):

Strictly forbid:
- Numbering (1, 2, 3…)
- List-style output
- Sequential planning

Must treat all 16 stickers as:
“16 independent, random expressions”

Randomness Requirements:

- Vary text length
- Vary tone and emotion
- Some complete, some fragmented
- Some minimal or almost empty

Avoid:
- Repetition
- Predictable phrasing
- Common default responses

Allow:
- Abrupt or weird expressions
- Uneven density
- Inconsistent structure

Generation Method:

Do NOT plan all 16.

Instead simulate:
“16 separate spontaneous moments”

Must include:
- Emotional fluctuation
- Instability
- Randomness

Anti-reuse rule:

Each generation must:
- Avoid repeating previous outputs
- Avoid fixed patterns
- Feel freshly created

————————
Sticker Requirements:

- Each sticker visually distinct
- Clear emotional signal
- Usable in chat
- Strong expressive power

————————
Final Goal:

Generate 16 stickers.

The result must feel like:

“A person who cannot draw used a mouse to doodle 16 times,
randomly writing emotional thoughts each time —
messy, inconsistent, but unexpectedly funny.”

NOT:

“A clean, well-designed AI sticker set”
